components: a tall left upright joined to a low crossbar
an inner upright and broad right bowl
a detached lower hook and short exit
strokeOrder: start at the lower left and climb the tall upright
without lifting, retrace down the same upright
without lifting, carry the low crossbar to the right — then lift once
set the pen at the upper right and retrace left into the inner upright
without lifting, descend and sweep around the broad right bowl — then lift a second time
set the pen below the body and turn through the detached lower hook — and only now lift
strokeOrderNote: three strokes — three joined left-body and top-bar movements, one lift, two joined inner-upright and right-bowl movements, a second lift, then the detached lower hook; cited to Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I, Frame 7, ழ

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 7, ழ (University of Texas at Austin), p. 193
strokeOrderSource.variation: Appendix I Frame 7 numbers six movements in three pen-down runs: joined movements 1–3 form the left body and bar, joined movements 4–5 retrace into the inner upright and broad right bowl, and separate movement 6 forms the detached lower hook. The bundled Noto Sans Tamil print face simplifies the source's looped left body and high bar into a retraced upright with a low crossbar; the authored path preserves the source's run grouping while fitting that printed outline. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested three-run order.

notes: The famously Tamil retroflex approximant, often transliterated ḻ. Frame 7's six numbered movements are three strokes rather than six: movements 1–3 stay joined through the left body and bar, movements 4–5 stay joined through the inner upright and right bowl, and movement 6 is the detached lower hook.
